Looking at the dot cell, its only neighbors in the shape are the cell to its right and the cell below it — and each of those two cells has *no other* neighbors in the shape. So whichever piece covers the dot must also cover both of those "leaf" cells, forming a corner shape.

- Piece A (straight tromino) can't form a corner.
- Piece D (2×2 square) would need a fourth cell diagonally placed, which isn't in the shape.
- Piece B (L-tetromino) would need its long arm to extend beyond a leaf cell, impossible here.
- Piece E (F-pentomino) would require the dot cell to have four piece-neighbors (a cross), which doesn't match E.
- Piece C (T-tetromino) fits perfectly: dot cell as center, with the two leaves and one more cell completing the T.

A complete tiling confirms this: C = {dot, right leaf, bottom leaf, left neighbor}, D = the 2×2 block at bottom-left, E = the region at top-right including the upper-right corner, B = the top-left L, A = the middle horizontal strip.

Thus the piece on the dot is C.
